title: The One-Way Door Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
Aarav puts batteries into his bike lamp and nothing happens. He flips them and it shines. Inside is a diode, a p-n junction that lets current through one way only. We start with a heavy swing door with a strong spring and a doorstep, then see the real thing: in forward bias (p to +) the barrier gets lower and the depletion layer thinner; in reverse bias (p to -) the barrier gets higher, the layer wider, and only a tiny minority-carrier current leaks through.

On a live breadboard a supply knob sweeps the voltage while the readout and the live V-I plot trace the full curve: almost no current below the knee, a sharp rise near the cut-in voltage (about 0.7 V for silicon, about 0.2 V for germanium), a flat microampere leak in reverse and the sudden rise at breakdown. Then dynamic resistance, r_d = delta V / delta I, with a worked example above the knee (5 ohms forward vs ten million ohms reverse), the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 41 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits | ISC Class 12 Physics: Electronic Devices (semiconductor diode, I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias).
